1.א: Liability for cooking on Shabbat: Mishnah Kelal Gadol (Shabbat 73b) lists “… kneading and baking” among avot; the Gemara questions where healing spices in the Mishkan fit, answers the Tanna gave the sequence of bread preparation and put baking in the “cooking” slot—hence bishul is a principal melakhah for chatat.
1.ב: Who may eat, shogeg/mezid, and whether all melakhot follow one rule: Rif Kirah paskens R. Yehudah; Geonim; Bach infers R. Yoḥanan like R. Meir, hence “no distinction in any Shabbat act.” Baal HaTerumot limits R. Meir’s heter of eating shogeg-cooked food; Ra’ash Chullin explains divergent rules if following R. Meir vs. R. Yehudah. Bach concludes practice follows R. Yehudah like Tur/Shulchan Aruch.
1.ג: Mezid—for others no “bdei sheyeasu” when a Jew cooks for himself (Rambam; Ein Tzedin / Eruvin precedents); rationale differs from “bdei” after Gentile work. One who cooks for a dangerously ill patient—healthy people may eat Motza’ei without waiting because we do not treat permitted life-saving labor as forbidden benefit that day (see Beit Yosef citing Rashba).

2.ד: Shechitah for a patient on Shabbat: Tur follows Rav Dimi (Chullin 15a) permitting healthy eaters in the innards even if the animal fell ill that day; Ra’ash explains muktzeh does not apply because we follow R. Shimon unless food was actively rejected (muktzeh middeissura needs discarding + unsuitability).
2.ה: “Without salting”: Tosafot—forbidden to salt on Shabbat (salting hides is an av melakhah); permitted to eat unsalted raw meat—blood absorbed in the meat without discharge carries no Torah prohibition even rabbinically.

3.ו: Solar derivatives forbidden like fire—Mishnah/Gemara Shabbat Kirah; halakhah follows first Tanna who decrees solar heat lest confusion with fire (not like R. Yosei who permits pure solar cooking).
3.ז: Burying on chol and rolling on sand—Gemara: even R. Yosei forbids burying in sand (Rabba: lest ash burial; R. Yosef: lest move soil); Ra’ash extends to rolling on sand to roast; Bach asks why Tur omitted explicit twilight prohibition when Rabba would forbid.

4.ח: Fully cooked stew reheated—major analysis of Shabbat 34b (“shema yirte’aḥ”), Ra’ash vs. Rashi whether “reheat” creates Torah bishul after full cooking; distinction ben drusai vs. fully cooked; comparison to Mishnah Ḥavit “anything coming hot erev”; Bach’s halakhic conclusion follows Rashi/Rambam that Torah bishul can apply while liquid dish still boiling until fully cooked/cooled dynamics; ties to Rema about qualitative improvement (“metzamek ve-yafeh lo”).

5.ט: Salt/bread/keli sheni: lengthy survey of Ra’ah, Semag/Semak, Mordekhai Pesahim (“roast then boil”), Rabbeinu Yaakov’s question, Tosafot harmonizing shelakot berakhot vs. Pesah/matzah; Bach reconciles Ra’ah stringency with keli sheni general rule; BY’s discussion of Peredeṣ (old salted fish) and practical caution.

9.י: Keli rishon after removal from fire—Mishnah Kirah; Ra’ash on meat/salt/moisture/blood absorption and dual relevance to Shabbat vs. blood prohibition; apparent contradiction between Ra’ash opening (“permitted raw meat”) and Rema’s salted meat gloss—Bach navigates Beit Yosef, Hagahot SA, Tosafot on Keli Sheni blood absorption; exhaustive analysis of basin/bathing vessels vs. drinking vessels, Gemara sugya (Abaye/Rava/R. Ḥiyya), Tosafot on keli sheni definition, BY’s attempt to explain Tur’s rulings on pouring cold/hot water; lengthy critique of Rambam/BY on bathhouse vessels and correct girsa “keli sheni”; minority vs. majority mixtures (Beit Shammai/Hillel patterns); “tatah gavar” vs. appearance of cooking; concludes stringent like Bach’s reading of Ra’ash for moisture cases.

11.יג: Tur’s ruling on basin cold/hot water—Bach finds Gemara (spal ke-amḥti) puzzling; develops Tosafot theory distinguishing washing basin from drinking vessel and Rema’s rulings on pouring.
11.יד: Why decree cooking-appearance for bathing vessels but not cups—because bathwater is extremely hot onlookers confuse keli rishon vs. sheni.
11.טו: Further difficulties tying Beit Shammai/Hillel pouring patterns to Tur’s language—lengthy reconciliation of “tatah gavar,” majority/minority mixtures, Rambam’s rulings; argues BY sometimes misread HaMagid’s gloss on Rambam’s bathhouse kelim.

12.יא: Copper kettle Mishnah—Shmuel permits davar she-eino mitkaven even if kettle joins (not pesik reisha to forbidden tziruf); Tosafot/Ran; fixing keli unintentionally exempt.
12.יב: Cup with hot water—Bach explains Tur following Tosafot Beit Shammai/Hillel: minority hot into majority cold doesn’t cook; Rema permits keli sheni patterns accordingly.

14.טז: Beraita jug opposite fire oil/water—BY favors Tosafot/Ra’ash over Rashi/Rambam on whether oil “cooks”; “yad soledes” defined by infant-scald test for wine/oil.

16.יז: Pashtida/anpanda—BY lengthy discussion; Sefer HaMitzvot permits; Shulchan Aruch follows lenient view; Hagahot SA notes practice to be stringent but in need may rely on lenient opinions.
